samples.summary: `buildProgram()` runs in the default-parameter position, outside `runCli`'s try/catch, so a throw during program construction escapes as an unhandled rejection instead of the error envelope
samples.evidence: `export async function runCli(program: Command = buildProgram(), ...)` (cli.ts:49-52) evaluates `buildProgram()` during parameter binding, before the `try { await program.parseAsync(...) } catch { outputError(e) }` body at lines 53-57. Because `runCli` is `async`, a throw there rejects the returned promise; `bin.ts:6` does `void runCli()` with no `.catch`, so any failure inside `createProgram()`/`register*Command()` (e.g. commander throwing on a duplicate option/command name, or `version` being missing) terminates the process with a raw unhandled-rejection stack trace rather than the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope the CLI contract promises. Moving the default-argument resolution inside the try (e.g. `program?: Command` then `const p = program ?? buildProgram()` inside the try) would close it. Behaviourally similar to the pre-change top-level construction in bin.ts, so this is a carried-over gap rather than a new regression, but the delta is the point where construction became catchable and did not.

samples.summary: If the `vi.mock('../src/cli.js')` stub ever fails to apply, importing `src/bin.ts` executes the real CLI against vitest's `process.argv`, and commander's default error path calls `process.exit(1)`, killing the test worker instead of failing the assertion
samples.evidence: `await import('../src/bin.js')` (bin.test.ts:15) relies entirely on the hoisted mock at line 11. `packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:42` builds the program with no `exitOverride()`, so on an unknown argument commander calls `process.exit`. With the real module loaded, `void runCli()` in bin.ts:6 would parse vitest's argv and hard-exit the worker — an opaque failure mode rather than a red test. Adding `program.exitOverride()` in the test path, or asserting on an injected argv, avoids it. Flagged for the runtime-behaviour aspect (process-killing side effect on import); the test-design aspect belongs to the test lens.
